thread.title: Apple Is Easy For Shareholders - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Michael Wiggins De Oliveira
title: Apple Is Easy For Shareholders - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Investment Thesis The best investments are those where, opposite to popular opinion, one does not have to be the smartest person in the room. The best investments are ones where the odds of success are so far tilted to one’s favor that even if so much can be wrong in one thesis, you still end up doing quite well. Apple ( AAPL ) is the elephant in the room, which offers investors a great investment opportunity, without having to be too smart.
Built-In Discount From Value Apple's shares have picked up some steam of late. Given that Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A ) ( BRK.B ) has also noticed the bargain opportunity, and has been very vocal about it, this will have motivated many investors to join the party.
However, if we start from afar, we can see why Apple makes fantastic sense. Not only to the flagship of experienced value investors, as in Berkshire, but to retail investors too. As of Q2 2018 , Apple has a net cash position of just over $150 billion, implying that around 15% of Apple's market cap is made up of cash. Said another way, investors are getting a discount from its market cap just because of the strength of its balance sheet.
Maestri Is Confident Next, on to share repurchases. CFO Maestri had been firm all the way up to Q1 2018 , stating that Apple was going to deploy its war chest 'slowly over time', favoring what he described as, 'patient and long-term investors', rather than Apple deploying its large amounts of cash quickly. Then, just 90 days later, Apple announced a new $100 billion share repurchase plan. After near enough completing on its previous $200 billion of repurchases, this new announcement came out. Given that Apple's previous repurchase plan, which started from August 2012, is expected to complete at some point during the Q3 2018, and that Apple is forging on ahead with a new repurchase plan, it certainly speaks of the confidence of one of the most prudent companies on Wall Street.
New Era Business Model Apple has a history of reinventing itself. It seems very difficult to believe that just 11 years ago, the iPhone was hardly well known outside a group of investors and geeks. Now Apple's active installed base exceeds 1.3 billion. On the other hand, the market for iPhone devices has obviously started to saturate, causing many investors to think that Apple is no longer a growth company. However, Apple's phenomenal team has not rested on its laurels; Apple has come up with a new business model away from the capital-intensive hardware business model it previously had - its Services .
At the end of Q2 2018, Apple's Services accounted for roughly 15% of its total revenue. However, what makes this revenue stream so valuable is that it not only leads to better profit margins, which will drive shareholders returns, but also that this revenue stream is more predictable and recurring - which together will cause investors to reappraise Apple’s valuation with a higher multiple to earnings.
Incidentally, Apple’s Services continued to advance at a strong clip and was up 31% YoY. Apple's Services is made up of sales of Apple's digital content, such as iTunes Store, App Store, and Apple Music, with smaller contributions from other sources. Moreover, what makes this business line truly remarkable is the ability of Apple to continue to ramp up the number of subscribers to its platform – given that subscribers are the holy grail of any business.

On the face of it, the above table does not depict Apple as a phenomenal investment opportunity. However, as discussed above, Apple's stock should reappraise significantly higher over time, driven in part by its Services segment, which delivers better margins and will drive Apple's consolidated profit margins higher, as Services continues to grow, become better known in the investment community and gradually become a larger part of Apple.
For instance, many investors value Amazon ( AMZN ) extremely highly for the fact that they know it well and regularly use its products. They argue that 'Amazon is everywhere' and that this reason alone makes Amazon a great investment. And if that thesis fails, then pointing out its rapidly rising share price becomes vindication that their argument is right, that Amazon is indeed a great investment. However, I argue that in a bull market many investments tend to get slightly irrationally priced. However, Apple continues to show that it is not only able to grow and monetize its core product very successfully, but that it is still able to reinvent and pivot its business to new growth areas.
Takeaway
We don’t have an analytical advantage, we just look in the right place.
– Seth Klarman
The best investors don’t try to overcomplicate the simple. Investing in this mega-cap, with its rock-solid balance sheet, led by a great management team and not having to overpay for its stock, makes a lot of sense.
